#Nirvana in Flames Wraps Filming# 
Someone once asked me why I chose Qin Changge, and why I chose Nirvana in Flames in the end. What first drew me in wasn't where the story would go, or who Changge would become — it was a very simple question: what does a person have to go through to become who she is now?

For a long stretch of preparation, I didn't know how to get close to her. Once filming began, she felt even further away than I'd imagined. Much of the time in between, I felt I still hadn't become her… until one day, as I said a certain line, I felt her state of mind at the very start of the story. From that moment, I seemed to finally find the inevitability in the course of her fate.

What Changge left me wasn't an answer, but a very quiet strength. She rarely rushes to prove herself or explain her motives — like a silent traveler who just keeps walking forward.

These few months together were truly worth it. I drew closer to her, and she slowly changed me too.

Thank you, Nirvana in Flames, and thank you to everyone who completed this story together — the director, the screenwriters, all my fellow actors, and every member of the crew behind the scenes; and thank you to the platform and production company for giving us this chance to meet. It's because of everyone's work that Qin Changge truly came to life.

If she can really hear me, I want to tell her: because of this story, more and more people in this world will understand you.

I hope you know.

Thank you for handing me all of that silence, restraint, judgement and fighting back these past months — for letting "growing up" happen not through slogans, but through one choice after another.

You are not strong because pain shaped you;
you got here through clarity, through a sense of measure, through refusing to back down again and again.

Thank you for showing me: not being controlled is not the same as winning; being able to redefine yourself is the real way out.

This journey ends here.
May you never have to prove anything again,
and never again need pain to remember who you are.

Thank you to everyone who let Zhou Yan breathe on this journey —
to Youku and Dunqi Studio for their full support of the work, so that such a complex and powerful character could be taken seriously and portrayed with care, with enough space for expression;

to director Gao Bingquan for his precise grasp of the character, keeping the restraint, the pauses and the subtle shifts in the frame;

to action director Chen Jiafu for his exacting standards on every movement, so that each action served the character and created a force field that belongs to "Origin" alone;

to the art team for building such immersive spaces, turning the "Gate of Rebirth" from a concept into something you can touch;

and to all my fellow actors —
the emotional bond of the "little brother and sister", the boundaries of order built by the "police team", the dramatic tension given by the "gang of thieves" — all of it gave Zhou Yan a complete, believable foundation in a world between magic and reality.

On this journey, Zhou Yan has reached her exit.

At this moment, may 《Be Reborn: Origin》 break through every door, stare into the abyss and find life.

Zhou Yan, happy wrap — I hope we meet again before long.

hy-RlKMS0Ykv.t: The story of Kill Me Love Me is about to end, so let me say goodbye to Mei Lin — she is sharp and stubborn, which is why, ten years ago, the little "beggar" of Qingzhou went without hesitation to assassinate her "enemy", the Butcher General; she is clever and clear-headed — as a death warrior she "fears death" but knows she "cannot die", and she can choose to uphold peace between two nations, urging Jing to move "forward"; she is kind and sensitive, she receives every bit of kindness around her and has the strength to give back even more; she is free-spirited — sincere and devoted to the love she has chosen, stubbornly guarding the ray of light behind her, and after all the love and hate she can choose to let go, change her name and live for herself. People say she is like the "never-die" flower blooming on ruins, and like fireworks bursting in the night. Some time ago a journalist asked me: if she were reborn or lived in a parallel world, would Mei Lin make up for the regrets of this life? I think Mei Lin wouldn't feel any regret — she hated to the fullest, loved to the fullest, tried to the fullest, and was free in being true to her heart; she lived this one life to the full! The snow of Qingzhou falls and falls; Mei Lin's lifelong wish is fulfilled, and she asks for nothing more. Mei Lin, goodbye.

One day at about ten in the morning, in a corner of the Court of State Ceremonial, Mei Lin wandered aimlessly down a corridor, not knowing where she was going. She turned her head and saw flowers, grass and a lake; sunlight fell right on her face. She slowed her steps and looked at everything, and for the first time felt a moment that belonged to her alone. She didn't want to lose herself in it, nor did she try to hold on to it; she just kept looking. She didn't know what she loved — that love was buried very, very deep in her heart, and it took the story of 《Kill Me Love Me》 for it to slowly surface, from blurry to clearer and clearer…
"Chun" (spring) is the middle character of her mother's name, Liu Chunxi. It is the "sprouting" and "life" of the story.
"Hua" (flower) is the love in her heart. It is the "hope" of the story.
"Yan" is everything the story holds.
Mei Lin walked into this story alone, and the gears began to turn; when we meet again, it will be the day the gears lock together.
"Lost and found again; a withered tree meets spring."

In one scene the lighting cue came in late, and Director Tian said, "Keep your eyes on your own work; know why you came here, and don't forget your original intention." Every role has things she can't help and things she says against her heart. Whether these roles succeed or fail, are loved or not recognised, I've given them my whole heart. But they shouldn't and can't imprison me, because I have more roles to create. Now that 《Knock on the Happiness Door》 has been airing for a while, there are some thoughts I'd like to share with you all.
First, please don't argue about "raising foreigners' children" in a show whose core and theme have nothing to do with nationality — it's really extreme. Mumu is first and foremost a life, a child who lost his parents. Faced with this child, two kind people chose to raise him rather than give up on him — I don't think that's something worth arguing about. Should they just stand by because he's mixed-race? Second, this script was my choice; it wasn't a filler show squeezed in because the schedule between 《Something Just Like This》 and 《Legacy》 was tight. It was the uniqueness of this role, something I'd never played before. And when I saw netizens say they didn't realise Fang Yan was played by Wei Yingluo's actress, I was really happy.
Finally, many people say I haven't had a hit since 《Story of Yanxi Palace》. Of course every actor hopes for a hit, and every crew member works their hardest for one. But what I care about more is learning something new and gaining something new through every new role.

Today is opening night, and Beijing is hazy. Right now I'm sitting in the dressing room, having just finished the first performance of our #抗战中的文艺#. Before the show we cheered each other on loudly backstage. My first time in a stage play — I couldn't hide how nervous and excited I was, so very nervous and so very excited. Once I stepped on stage and carried the character toward the audience, everything started going smoothly — that's the magic of the theatre.
Although it's my first time on the theatre stage, it's my second time working with Director Tian. Her professionalism and passion for theatre always inspire everyone around her. Her impression of me is that I can really endure long hours, and mine of her is the same — we clicked instantly. Our birthdays are just one day apart — a wonderful kind of fate. This time I felt her theatrical sharpness even more deeply; she always pinpoints our problems precisely and never holds back her praise. And with her leadership she takes care of lighting, stage design and every actor's issues. This morning she only came down from the stage after eleven, yet she never says she's tired, tirelessly making final adjustments to every detail. Without her there would be no play. She's like Superwoman, and I'm so grateful to work with her again.
This time I play the narrator of the chorus, as well as the senior performer Ms. Zhang Ruifang. Like the chorus part, Ms. Zhang's part combines the narrator's and her own perspective. In this performance I want to use the lines to show the contrast between a modern feel and the feel of that era, so the audience can step into Zhang Ruifang's story. In styling and way of speaking, I tried hard to recreate how things were back then, and I hope I can show the audience her frank, cheerful character and the strength of her pursuit of art.
Our first performance is done — great work, everyone! We were all brilliant! Thank you all, thank you for coming, and thank you to everyone on stage. 抗战中的文艺 — we continue tomorrow!

Written 2023.3.10:
Searching for the meaning of a lifetime ends up hurting yourself and others.
The injustice of the first half of life brought countless protectors.
A lifetime of searching for a home — where that home is, forgotten.
Who I am, forgotten; what I remember are the people.
All of you and all of them — and so there is me.
Written 2023.4.30:
Go, Xue Li — you can only move forward, because you can't go back. Head up, keep walking, keep climbing; the past will slowly fade away.
《The Double》 wraps, written 2023.9.19:
I've forgotten the road I came by; behind me there's only bright starlight.
Standing again at the crossroads of the ending, I look up and there's still a light.
Thank you for coming alone and giving this world a chance to love you again.
This world includes you yourself, and every bit of love in your shadow.
True to yourself, true to this life — may you always live free and passionate.

Xue Fangfei was unfortunate. She thought she had found a good man, only for her sincerity to be betrayed, and she nearly ended up like the line "in the human world the April blossoms are gone; a handful of earth, and no one knows".
Xue Fangfei was fortunate. On that stormy night on Qingcheng Mountain, she grabbed the vine of fate Jiang Li threw her and began the "script" of a new life. Shaking off the old frost and returning to the capital, at that moment she herself was the storm.
Xue Fangfei should have been a lone fighter swimming against the current, demanding justice from heaven, yet she was lucky to meet a group of people willing to stand behind her — Jiang Li, Tong'er, Qiongzhi, the mute old woman, the Ye family, her cousin from the Mingyi Hall squad, little Ruirui, Liu Xu, and Xiao Heng, who reached the same destination by a different road and is also where her heart belongs. They were Xue Fangfei's soft spot and also her armour. It was they who let Xue Fangfei grow through the ups and downs and finally find her way home.
In fact, everyone in the show, hero or villain, is just "a grain of sand in the torrent of the times", each with their own sorrow. Xue Fangfei's redemption began when she climbed out of the abyss of night; on the road of "looking back to ask about cause and effect, looking forward to demand justice", she gained along the way and lost along the way. Beneath the thrill lies utmost bitterness — it's precisely because of the thorny bitterness that cutting through the thorns feels so satisfying.
In recent interviews, journalists often asked me whether filming this kind of show felt especially satisfying. I always say that actually, I didn't find it satisfying. There were lots of scenes, lots of lines and a complex character; I had to keep brewing all kinds of emotions to adapt to the shifting plot, and also learn to rein them in and judge how much to show. Not knowing whether I could act it well, the pressure was actually huge. The whole process was exhausting, but also deeply fulfilling.
